deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is part of Riemann's student essay 'Versuch einer allgemeinen Auffassung der Integration und Differentiation' (dated 1847, published posthumously in the Werke, 1876). The previous page argues that a series of 'form (2)', running to infinity in both directions, can have a definite value even where term-by-term addition fails. To give an example, Riemann sets out to expand x^mu in a two-sided series of powers of (x-b). He also says he will need this expansion later in the investigation.

Step 1 (ansatz). Set z = x^mu = sum_{alpha=-oo}^{oo} c_alpha (x-b)^alpha. Presumably alpha runs over a progression alpha_0 + n with n in Z and alpha_0 possibly non-integer (my reading, from the context of form (2)).

Step 2 (Euler-type ODE). From z = x^mu we get z' = mu x^(mu-1), hence mu z - x z' = 0.

Step 3 (substitution). Write x = (x-b) + b. Then
mu z - x z' = sum mu c_alpha (x-b)^alpha - sum alpha c_alpha (x-b)^alpha - b sum alpha c_alpha (x-b)^(alpha-1).
Shifting the index in the last sum (my step) gives
sum_alpha [(mu-alpha) c_alpha - b(alpha+1) c_(alpha+1)] (x-b)^alpha = 0.

Step 4 (recursion). This condition is satisfied as soon as (mu-alpha) c_alpha = b(alpha+1) c_(alpha+1), i.e. c_(alpha+1)/c_alpha = (mu-alpha)/(b(alpha+1)).
- Riemann states this only as a sufficient condition.
- A struck-out fragment 'c_(alpha+1)=0' shows he was correcting as he wrote.
- Implicit solution (mine): c_alpha = C b^(-alpha) / (Gamma(alpha+1) Gamma(mu-alpha+1)), with C constant along the progression.
- For integer alpha this reduces to the binomial series c_n = binomial(mu,n) b^(mu-n) (up to K).

Step 5 (identifying the sum). Every solution of the ODE mu z - x z' = 0 is of the form K x^mu. So the series z obeying the recursion must equal K x^mu for some constant K, which remains to be found.

Step 6 (cutting the series). Split the series at index alpha:
- p = ... + c_(alpha-1)(x-b)^(alpha-1) + c_alpha (x-b)^alpha (the left tail);
- p' = c_(alpha+1)(x-b)^(alpha+1) + c_(alpha+2)(x-b)^(alpha+2) + ... (the right tail);
- so p + p' = z = K x^mu.

Step 7 (tails satisfy inhomogeneous ODEs). Applying the operator L = mu - x d/dx to each tail, the telescoping recursion kills all terms except one boundary term:
- L p = (mu-alpha) c_alpha (x-b)^alpha =: X;
- L p' = -b(alpha+1) c_(alpha+1) (x-b)^alpha = -X, using the recursion.

The page breaks off with the pencil note 'hier folgt gleich p. 9'. Presumably (my inference) Riemann next integrates the first-order ODE: (p x^(-mu))' = -X x^(-mu-1), so p = -x^mu * integral X x^(-mu-1) dx. This expresses the tails by Beta-type integrals and determines K.
errors: No algebraic errors: Step 3 (index shift) and both boundary-term computations in Step 7 are correct.

Unjustified step: termwise differentiation and rearrangement of a doubly infinite series is assumed. Such a series converges at best on |x-b| = |b|, since one tail has ratio (x-b)/b and the other b/(x-b). This is consistent with Riemann's stated willingness (previous page) to work with series whose value is not reached by term addition.

Gap in Step 5: 'all solutions are K x^mu' tacitly fixes a branch of x^mu on a connected domain. Also, the constancy of C along the index progression (versus a factor periodic in alpha) is left implicit.
The recursion is presented only as sufficient. That is logically fine for the argument, which needs only some series obeying it.

results.what: Two-sided (bilateral) expansion of x^mu in powers (x-b)^(alpha+n), n in Z, with coefficients fixed by (mu-alpha)c_alpha = b(alpha+1)c_(alpha+1), i.e. c_alpha proportional to b^(mu-alpha)/(Gamma(alpha+1)Gamma(mu-alpha+1))
results.modern_name: Riemann's generalized Taylor series / bilateral binomial series (fractional-index binomial expansion)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (Versuch, 1847, publ. 1876); later discussed by G. H. Hardy ('Riemann's form of Taylor's series', 1945)

results.what: Determining a series coefficient recursion from the Euler-type ODE mu z - x z' = 0 satisfied by x^mu
results.modern_name: Method of undetermined coefficients / recurrence from a linear ODE

results.what: Splitting the bilateral series into tails p, p'; each tail satisfies mu y - x y' = ±X with a single boundary term X = (mu-alpha)c_alpha(x-b)^alpha, to be solved by quadrature to find K
results.modern_name: Telescoping boundary term; first-order linear ODE / integrating-factor evaluation of series tails
results.usually_credited_to: standard technique; this specific use appears in Riemann's published Versuch

In the line 'Gesetz (mu-alpha)c_alpha - b(alpha+1)c_(alpha+1)=0' the struck-out fragment is 'c_(alpha+1)=0' at the start of the next line. The transcription handles this correctly.
